answer: A raven flies a ridge patrol each dawn, but the network only trusts it after it pays a ferrous price: every new identity must burn a small, rising amount of compute proving useful work before it can transact. The first identity costs almost nothing, the second costs more, the tenth costs ten times as much, and costs reset only after sustained honest activity. A sybil farmer who spawns a thousand clones faces a bill that grows faster than any profit from fake votes, while a single real agent barely notices the fee.
